general: Extract every entity of the supplied types. Return exact spans from the query. Leave other text unlabelled.
A1 Nationality, people and language adjectives such as "American", "Dutch", "Israeli", "English" are Other, never Country.

classes.name: Researcher
classes.description: Refers to an individual engaged in research activities within the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI), including professors, Ph.D. students, and researchers in academia, research institutions, and companies.
rules: RE1 If a person is involved in AI research, label them as a researcher entity instead of a person entity.

RE2 People described by research roles (elected fellow or member of a society, conference or program chair, journal editor, institute founder, developer of robots or software) are Researcher, also when only a surname or first name is given: "Sycara", "Mehler", "Hayes", "Miller", "Devol".
RE3 Examples: "Jürgen Schmidhuber", "Seymour Papert", "Victor Scheinman", "Scheinman", "X.Y. Feng".

classes.name: Country
rules: CO1 Examples: "Netherlands", "Japan", "Germany", "Canada", "Australia".

classes.name: Person
classes.description: Refers to an individual's name that is not a researcher.
rules: PE1 Person is only for people outside research, such as actors, film characters, directors, writers, athletes and politicians: "Harrison Ford", "Ridley Scott", "Lee Sedol".
PE2 Examples: "Francis Ford Coppola", "Michael Jackson", "John Wayne", "Rita Hayworth", "Dean Martin".

classes.name: Conference
classes.description: Refers to a research conference or journal in the field of Artificial Intelligence.
rules: CON1 This category includes conferences where AI research is presented and published.

CON2 Research societies of AI, computing and computational linguistics are Conference, not Organization: "Association for Computational Linguistics", "ACL", "AAAI", "Association for Computing Machinery", "ACM". Societies of other fields, such as "American Psychological Association" and "Cognitive Science Society", and "IEEE" stay Organization.
CON3 Their special interest groups and resource associations are Conference too: "Special Interest Group on Web as Corpus", "SIGWAC", "ELRA".
CON4 Examples: "AAAI", "1982 Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence", "SIGGRAPH", "Symposium on Geometry Processing", "International Journal of Computer Vision".

classes.name: Field
classes.description: Refers to a specific research area or subfield within Artificial Intelligence.
rules: FI1 Also annotate acronyms such as NLP.
FI2 Learning paradigms and mining areas are Field, not Task: "supervised learning", "semi-supervised learning", "text mining", "data mining".
FI3 Also label broad disciplines as Field: "computer science", "artificial intelligence", "mathematics", "statistics", "chemistry", "biology".
FI4 Examples: "deep learning", "pattern recognition", "image processing", "reinforcement learning", "natural language processing".

classes.name: Metric
classes.description: Refers to evaluation metrics used to assess the performance of AI models and algorithms.
rules: ME1 Annotate specific metrics like F1-score.
ME2 Also label these evaluation terms as Metric: "accuracy", "precision", "recall", "sensitivity", "specificity", "confusion matrix".
ME3 A ratio formula is one Metric span: "TP / ( TP + FP )", "FN / ( TN + FN )".
ME4 Examples: "mean squared error", "DCG", "maximum likelihood", "Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation", "MSE".

classes.name: Task
classes.description: Refers to a particular research task or problem within a specific AI research field.
rules: TA1 Annotate the name of the specific task, such as machine translation or object detection.
TA2 Concrete problems a system solves are Task, not Field: "object recognition", "object detection", "information retrieval", "speech perception", "OCR".
TA3 Sub-domains and applications listed under a field are Task: "scene reconstruction", "3D pose estimation", "audio signal processing", "video compression".
TA4 Examples: "speech synthesis", "information retrieval", "Feature extraction", "dimension reduction", "speech recognition".

classes.name: Other
classes.description: Refers to named entities that are not included in any other category.
rules: OT1 An award or prize is one Other span that includes the organization name and year in front of it: "NSF Career Award", "2018 Turing Award", "IEEE James L. Flanagan Speech and Audio Processing Award".
OT2 Also label as Other: "PhD", "IDE".
OT3 Examples: "unsupervised methods", "topological properties", "audio signal", "eigenfaces", "intelligent agents".

classes.name: Location
classes.description: Refers to a specific geographical or structural location.
rules: LO1 This includes but is not limited to: places (e.g., parks, landmarks), bridges, cities, towns, villages, areas and other distinct regions.
LO2 Examples: "Chișinău", "Paris", "Montreal", "Scotiabank Theatre Toronto", "TIFF Bell Lightbox".

classes.name: Algorithm
classes.description: Refers to an algorithmic procedure or computational model used in Artificial Intelligence research.
rules: AL1 This category includes algorithms (e.g., decision trees) and models (e.g., CNN and LSTM).
AL2 Estimation methods "maximum likelihood", "maximum a posteriori" and "MAP" are Algorithm, not Metric.
AL3 Also label these as Algorithm: "sigmoid function", "logistic function", "genetic algorithm", "convolution".
AL4 An Algorithm span keeps a following "algorithm", "method", "model" or "function": "EM algorithm", "Baum-Welch algorithm", "backpropagation algorithm", "maximum likelihood method".
AL5 Named techniques and procedures are Algorithm, not Task: "Collaborative filtering", "PCA whitening", "ZCA-whitening", "linear programming", "dynamic programming", "cross-validation".
AL6 Examples: "principal component analysis", "linear discriminant analysis", "gradient descent", "Support vector machine", "recurrent neural network".

classes.name: Product
classes.description: Refers to a product, system, or toolkit related to Artificial Intelligence.
rules: PR1 This includes specific AI-enabled products (e.g., robots like Pepper), systems (e.g., facial recognition systems), and toolkits (e.g., Tensorflow and PyTorch).
PR2 Named software, operating systems, devices, voice assistants and lexical databases are Product, not Other or ProgrammingLanguage: "WordNet", "Siri", "Android", "iPhone 4S", "Linux", "MATLAB".

PR3 A Product span keeps a following "system", "operating system", "toolkit", "API" or "package": "iOS operating system", "Sphinx toolkit", "Interlisp programming system", "interlingual machine translation system".
PR4 Also label these kinds of robots and systems as Product: "serial manipulator", "industrial robot", "recommender system", "chatbots".
PR5 Translation tools and processing modules are Product, not Task: "computer-aided translation", "machine-aided human translation", "coreference tagger", "Named entity recognition transducer".
PR6 Examples: "MATLAB", "Programmable Universal Machine for Assembly", "industrial robot", "opinion-based recommender system", "Octave".

classes.name: Organization
classes.description: Refers to a structured group, institution, company, or association.
rules: OR1 This category covers a diverse range of organizations, including businesses, non-profits, educational institutions, and government agencies.
OR2 Examples: "Unimation", "IAPR", "Audio Engineering Society", "National Science Foundation", "National Aeronautics and Space Administration".

classes.name: University
classes.description: Refers to an educational institution of higher learning.
rules: UN1 Label organizations that are universities as 'university'' entities.

UN2 Institutes and centres that are part of a university are University, not Organization: "Robotics Institute", "Human-Computer Interaction Institute", "Entertainment Technology Center", "Indian Statistical Institute".
UN3 Examples: "University of Toronto", "Cambridge", "University of Groningen", "MIT", "Brown University".

classes.name: ProgrammingLanguage
classes.description: Refers to a programming language used in the development of AI applications and research.
rules: PL1 Annotate the name of the programming language, such as Java and Python.
PL2 Examples: "Java", "R", "CLIPS", "Python", "C + +".
